prose--blog col-span-full!"><p>Cursor cloud agents can execute on dynamically scheduled pools of machines inside your network. You manage the underlying infrastructure, while agents are still started and managed from Cursor.</p>
<p>This gives teams more control over where agents execute and what infrastructure they use. Agents can work next to internal services and source control, run on custom hardware, or use operating systems and build pipelines that are difficult to package as a Cloud Agent build.</p>
<p>Cloud agents now create more than 60% of the pull requests we merge internally and are taking on a growing share of software work at many of the largest enterprises we work with. As their role expands, the machines they run on matter more too. These new capabilities make it practical for teams to provide and manage that infrastructure at scale.</p>
<div class="card mb-v2"><blockquote class="not-prose"><p class="type-base whitespace-pre-wrap">With Lambda MicroVMs as the compute layer for Cursor Cloud Agents, developers can run AI-powered coding agents in their own AWS account. Each machine launches near-instantly from a snapshot, suspends when idle, and resumes with full state. Your coding agents benefit from Lambda&#x27;s fast startup, strong isolation, and zero fleet management, while Cursor orchestrates the work.</p></blockquote><div class="mt-v1 flex items-center space-x-(--grid-gap)"><div><div class="type-sm">Ayush Kulkarni</div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text-sec">Senior Product Manager<!-- -->, <!-- -->AWS Lambda</div></div></div></div>
<h2 id="control-where-agents-execute" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#control-where-agents-execute" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Control where agents execute</h2>
<p>Cursor-hosted environments remain the default for cloud agents. Each session runs on a dedicated VM inside the Cursor cloud, with its dependencies installed and its own network controls. Per-agent isolation, secret redaction, egress controls, and signed commits meet the security requirements of most teams.</p>
<p>Teams generally use Self-Hosted Machines when:</p>
<ul>
<li>Agent tool execution needs to happen inside their network, with direct access to source control, internal services, and code repositories.</li>
<li>Agents require custom hardware, such as GPUs or Macs for iOS development, or infrastructure such as Kubernetes, sandboxes, or managed VMs.</li>
<li>Their operating system or build pipeline is difficult to package as a <a href="https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/builds" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">Cloud Agent build</a>.</li>
</ul>
<p>With Self-Hosted Machines, only the execution environment moves while the agent loop, inference, and planning remain in the Cursor cloud. Tool outputs flow back to Cursor for inference and may contain code, and agent transcripts may be processed and stored by Cursor. Teams can continue to access cloud agents from the desktop app, <a href="https://cursor.com/" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">cursor.com</a>, mobile, Slack, GitHub, and Linear.</p>
<figure><div class="media-border-container overflow-hidden"><img alt="Decision guide for when to use Self-Hosted Machines versus Cursor-hosted cloud agents" loading="lazy" width="800" height="450" decoding="async" data-nimg="1" class="media-light transition-opacity duration-[220ms] ease-[var(--ease-out-spring)] will-change-[opacity] opacity-0" style="color:transparent" srcSet="/marketing-static/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fptht05hbb1ssoooe.public.blob.vercel-storage.com%2Fassets%2Fblog%2Fcursor-self-hosted-decision-light-5mb0pPlah9XuRCmn3FSuKKPoaut0lr.png&amp;w=828&amp;q=70 1x, /marketing-static/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fptht05hbb1ssoooe.public.blob.vercel-storage.com%2Fassets%2Fblog%2Fcursor-self-hosted-decision-light-5mb0pPlah9XuRCmn3FSuKKPoaut0lr.png&amp;w=1920&amp;q=70 2x" src="/marketing-static/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fptht05hbb1ssoooe.public.blob.vercel-storage.com%2Fassets%2Fblog%2Fcursor-self-hosted-decision-light-5mb0pPlah9XuRCmn3FSuKKPoaut0lr.png&amp;w=1920&amp;q=70"/><img alt="Decision guide for when to use Self-Hosted Machines versus Cursor-hosted cloud agents" loading="lazy" width="800" height="450" decoding="async" data-nimg="1" class="media-dark transition-opacity duration-[220ms] ease-[var(--ease-out-spring)] will-change-[opacity] opacity-0" style="color:transparent" srcSet="/marketing-static/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fptht05hbb1ssoooe.public.blob.vercel-storage.com%2Fassets%2Fblog%2Fcursor-self-hosted-decision-dark-9pFJZSGCD6lu2MsDVRw6WazC2hLuf7.png&amp;w=828&amp;q=70 1x, /marketing-static/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fptht05hbb1ssoooe.public.blob.vercel-storage.com%2Fassets%2Fblog%2Fcursor-self-hosted-decision-dark-9pFJZSGCD6lu2MsDVRw6WazC2hLuf7.png&amp;w=1920&amp;q=70 2x" src="/marketing-static/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fptht05hbb1ssoooe.public.blob.vercel-storage.com%2Fassets%2Fblog%2Fcursor-self-hosted-decision-dark-9pFJZSGCD6lu2MsDVRw6WazC2hLuf7.png&amp;w=1920&amp;q=70"/></div></figure>
<h2 id="workers-connect-your-infrastructure-to-the-cursor-agent-loop" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#workers-connect-your-infrastructure-to-the-cursor-agent-loop" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Workers connect your infrastructure to the Cursor agent loop</h2>
<p>With Self-Hosted Machines, tool execution moves from a Cursor-hosted VM to a machine in your environment. That machine holds the working copy of the repository, edits files, and runs commands. A worker connects it to the rest of the agent system.</p>
<p>To register a machine, run a worker by installing the Cursor CLI and running <code>agent worker start</code>. This opens a long-lived outbound HTTPS connection to the Cursor cloud. When a session begins, Cursor&#x27;s agent harness handles inference and planning, then sends tool calls to a dedicated worker for execution. The worker returns the results for the next round of inference. Cursor never initiates a connection into your network.</p>
<figure><div class="media-border-container overflow-hidden"><img alt="Architecture diagram showing the Cursor agent loop in the cloud and tool execution on a worker in your network" loading="lazy" width="800" height="450" decoding="async" data-nimg="1" class="media-light transition-opacity duration-[220ms] ease-[var(--ease-out-spring)] will-change-[opacity] opacity-0" style="color:transparent" srcSet="/marketing-static/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fptht05hbb1ssoooe.public.blob.vercel-storage.com%2Fassets%2Fblog%2Fcursor-agent-loop-light-GMamDuzZU5LzYrpQOhRxRwBvrbhRFg.png&amp;w=828&amp;q=70 1x, /marketing-static/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fptht05hbb1ssoooe.public.blob.vercel-storage.com%2Fassets%2Fblog%2Fcursor-agent-loop-light-GMamDuzZU5LzYrpQOhRxRwBvrbhRFg.png&amp;w=1920&amp;q=70 2x" src="/marketing-static/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fptht05hbb1ssoooe.public.blob.vercel-storage.com%2Fassets%2Fblog%2Fcursor-agent-loop-light-GMamDuzZU5LzYrpQOhRxRwBvrbhRFg.png&amp;w=1920&amp;q=70"/><img alt="Architecture diagram showing the Cursor agent loop in the cloud and tool execution on a worker in your network" loading="lazy" width="800" height="450" decoding="async" data-nimg="1" class="media-dark transition-opacity duration-[220ms] ease-[var(--ease-out-spring)] will-change-[opacity] opacity-0" style="color:transparent" srcSet="/marketing-static/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fptht05hbb1ssoooe.public.blob.vercel-storage.com%2Fassets%2Fblog%2Fcursor-agent-loop-dark-qmfnmGC3l8Rw7858QUDT6xB8OuzndD.png&amp;w=828&amp;q=70 1x, /marketing-static/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fptht05hbb1ssoooe.public.blob.vercel-storage.com%2Fassets%2Fblog%2Fcursor-agent-loop-dark-qmfnmGC3l8Rw7858QUDT6xB8OuzndD.png&amp;w=1920&amp;q=70 2x" src="/marketing-static/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fptht05hbb1ssoooe.public.blob.vercel-storage.com%2Fassets%2Fblog%2Fcursor-agent-loop-dark-qmfnmGC3l8Rw7858QUDT6xB8OuzndD.png&amp;w=1920&amp;q=70"/></div></figure>
<figure><div class="media-border-container overflow-hidden"><img alt="Deployment options for cloud agents: Cursor-hosted machines or workers on your servers and public cloud" loading="lazy" width="800" height="450" decoding="async" data-nimg="1" class="media-light transition-opacity duration-[220ms] ease-[var(--ease-out-spring)] will-change-[opacity] opacity-0" style="color:transparent" srcSet="/marketing-static/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fptht05hbb1ssoooe.public.blob.vercel-storage.com%2Fassets%2Fblog%2Fcursor-deployment-options-light-eAVYesILhwbRYnoTFlTDJ4dvUWMszn.png&amp;w=828&amp;q=70 1x, /marketing-static/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fptht05hbb1ssoooe.public.blob.vercel-storage.com%2Fassets%2Fblog%2Fcursor-deployment-options-light-eAVYesILhwbRYnoTFlTDJ4dvUWMszn.png&amp;w=1920&amp;q=70 2x" src="/marketing-static/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fptht05hbb1ssoooe.public.blob.vercel-storage.com%2Fassets%2Fblog%2Fcursor-deployment-options-light-eAVYesILhwbRYnoTFlTDJ4dvUWMszn.png&amp;w=1920&amp;q=70"/><img alt="Deployment options for cloud agents: Cursor-hosted machines or workers on your servers and public cloud" loading="lazy" width="800" height="450" decoding="async" data-nimg="1" class="media-dark transition-opacity duration-[220ms] ease-[var(--ease-out-spring)] will-change-[opacity] opacity-0" style="color:transparent" srcSet="/marketing-static/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fptht05hbb1ssoooe.public.blob.vercel-storage.com%2Fassets%2Fblog%2Fcursor-deployment-options-dark-OZ0kFHszAKB8T4YViL8fRHBnuHnRGw.png&amp;w=828&amp;q=70 1x, /marketing-static/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fptht05hbb1ssoooe.public.blob.vercel-storage.com%2Fassets%2Fblog%2Fcursor-deployment-options-dark-OZ0kFHszAKB8T4YViL8fRHBnuHnRGw.png&amp;w=1920&amp;q=70 2x" src="/marketing-static/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fptht05hbb1ssoooe.public.blob.vercel-storage.com%2Fassets%2Fblog%2Fcursor-deployment-options-dark-OZ0kFHszAKB8T4YViL8fRHBnuHnRGw.png&amp;w=1920&amp;q=70"/></div></figure>
<p>Workers can be configured in two ways.</p>
<ol>
<li><strong>My Machines.</strong> This configuration connects a single laptop or VM to your account and is best suited to personal workflows.</li>
<li><strong>Pools.</strong> A pool is a named queue of workers that can serve a team or enterprise. Capacity increases as requests arrive and decreases after workers disconnect, letting your existing cloud infrastructure scale with developer demand.</li>
</ol>
<div class="card mb-v2"><blockquote class="not-prose"><p class="type-base whitespace-pre-wrap">Developers should have the flexibility to run coding agents on the platform that best supports their workflow, and companies should not have to compromise on control of where agents run and what they can access. The future of development will be built on powerful agents, running in secure, isolated environments.</p></blockquote><div class="mt-v1 flex items-center space-x-(--grid-gap)"><div><div class="type-sm">Meagan Gamache</div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text-sec">Director of Product Management, Developer Platforms<!-- -->, <!-- -->Cloudflare</div></div></div></div>
<h2 id="cloud-agents-adapt-to-your-infrastructure" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#cloud-agents-adapt-to-your-infrastructure" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Cloud agents adapt to your infrastructure</h2>
<p>Worker pools can now scale in response to queued requests and serve work from any repository. We have also added support for several sandbox providers and computer use on Linux alongside Mac.</p>
<h3 id="pools-scale-with-demand-and-serve-any-repository" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#pools-scale-with-demand-and-serve-any-repository" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Pools scale with demand and serve any repository</h3>
<p>Demand for cloud agents often arrives in bursts and Self-Hosted Machines pools adjust to those bursts automatically. This happens through a controller which watches the request queue and uses a spawn script supplied by the team to start machines as needed.</p>
<p>If a pool has an available worker, that worker claims the request. Otherwise, the request waits until more capacity becomes available, so teams do not have to decide how many machines to leave running.</p>
<p>Teams can set an idle timeout for each worker connection. Once it expires, the machine can reset and re-enter the pool. Teams can also preserve its workspace in case the agent receives a follow-up.</p>
<div class="card mb-v2"><blockquote class="not-prose"><p class="type-base whitespace-pre-wrap">Self-Hosted Machines put teams in control of where Cursor agents run, and Vercel Sandbox makes it effortless. Every task gets an isolated sandbox on demand, no fleet to manage, and nothing sitting idle.</p></blockquote><div class="mt-v1 flex items-center space-x-(--grid-gap)"><div><div class="type-sm">Allen Zhou</div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text-sec">Member of Technical Staff<!-- -->, <!-- -->Vercel</div></div></div></div>
<p>Leaving a machine running while its agent is idle can be expensive. But if the machine is released, the agent may need several minutes to reconstruct its workspace when a follow-up arrives. With hibernation, teams can snapshot and stop an idle machine instead. If a follow-up arrives within the reconnect window, the snapshot is restored and a worker starts with the same ID. Otherwise, the request can move to a new machine.</p>
<p>Pools are not tied to individual repositories. A request only needs to identify the pool, and any available worker can claim it. This lets one pool serve many repositories.</p>
<h3 id="workers-run-across-supported-sandbox-providers" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#workers-run-across-supported-sandbox-providers" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Workers run across supported sandbox providers</h3>
<p>Self-Hosted Machines does not require building a custom sandbox layer from scratch. We partner with <a href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/microvms-integrations-cursor-self-hosted-machines.html" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">AWS Lambda</a>, <a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/sandbox/tutorials/cursor-cloud-agents/" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">Cloudflare</a>, <a href="https://coder.com/docs/ai-coder/agent-relay/cursor" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">Coder</a>, <a href="https://daytona.io/docs/en/guides/cursor/cursor-self-hosted-machines" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">Daytona</a>, <a href="https://docs.e2b.dev/agents/cursor" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">E2B</a>, <a href="https://modal.com/docs/cursor" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">Modal</a>, <a href="https://namespace.so/docs/integrations/cursor" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">Namespace</a>, and <a href="https://vercel.com/kb/guide/cursor-vercel-sandbox" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">Vercel</a>, allowing workers to be started and orchestrated wherever a team&#x27;s sandboxes already run.</p>
<div class="card mb-v2"><blockquote class="not-prose"><p class="type-base whitespace-pre-wrap">Cursor Self-Hosted Machines on Modal gives each Cloud Agent session a Modal Sandbox, so you can hand it a machine tailor-made for its task.</p></blockquote><div class="mt-v1 flex items-center space-x-(--grid-gap)"><div><div class="type-sm">Adam Azzam</div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text-sec">Member of Product Staff<!-- -->, <!-- -->Modal</div></div></div></div>
<h3 id="agents-control-browsers-on-linux-and-mac" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#agents-control-browsers-on-linux-and-mac" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Agents control browsers on Linux and Mac</h3>
<p>Linux workers now support computer use alongside Macs. With the required <a href="https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/self-hosted/computer-use" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">computer use</a> dependencies installed, including Chrome or Chromium, an agent can click, take screenshots, and control the browser. You can watch its desktop or take control directly from Cursor.</p>
<div class="card mb-v2"><blockquote class="not-prose"><p class="type-base whitespace-pre-wrap">You can&#x27;t build iOS or macOS apps without a Mac. Namespace Devboxes spin up a real Mac for each Cursor Cloud Agent, which can now perform that work on Apple silicon.</p></blockquote><div class="mt-v1 flex items-center space-x-(--grid-gap)"><div><div class="type-sm">Hugo Santos</div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text-sec">CEO<!-- -->, <!-- -->Namespace</div></div></div></div>
<h2 id="bring-cloud-agents-into-your-environment" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#bring-cloud-agents-into-your-environment" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Bring cloud agents into your environment</h2>
<p>Teams have spent years shaping their infrastructure around how they build software. Self-Hosted Machines lets cloud agents fit more naturally into it, and we&#x27;re excited to see how far teams take them.</p>
<p>To connect a machine or configure a pool, <a href="https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/self-hosted" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">get started in the docs</a>.</p></div><footer prose--blog col-span-full!"><p>Cursor cloud agents can execute on dynamically scheduled pools of machines inside your network. You manage the underlying infrastructure, while agents are still started and managed from Cursor.</p>
<p>This gives teams more control over where agents execute and what infrastructure they use. Agents can work next to internal services and source control, run on custom hardware, or use operating systems and build pipelines that are difficult to package as a Cloud Agent build.</p>
<p>Cloud agents now create more than 60% of the pull requests we merge internally and are taking on a growing share of software work at many of the largest enterprises we work with. As their role expands, the machines they run on matter more too. These new capabilities make it practical for teams to provide and manage that infrastructure at scale.</p>
<div class="card mb-v2"><blockquote class="not-prose"><p class="type-base whitespace-pre-wrap">With Lambda MicroVMs as the compute layer for Cursor Cloud Agents, developers can run AI-powered coding agents in their own AWS account. Each machine launches near-instantly from a snapshot, suspends when idle, and resumes with full state. Your coding agents benefit from Lambda&#x27;s fast startup, strong isolation, and zero fleet management, while Cursor orchestrates the work.</p></blockquote><div class="mt-v1 flex items-center space-x-(--grid-gap)"><div><div class="type-sm">Ayush Kulkarni</div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text-sec">Senior Product Manager<!-- -->, <!-- -->AWS Lambda</div></div></div></div>
<h2 id="control-where-agents-execute" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#control-where-agents-execute" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Control where agents execute</h2>
<p>Cursor-hosted environments remain the default for cloud agents. Each session runs on a dedicated VM inside the Cursor cloud, with its dependencies installed and its own network controls. Per-agent isolation, secret redaction, egress controls, and signed commits meet the security requirements of most teams.</p>
<p>Teams generally use Self-Hosted Machines when:</p>
<ul>
<li>Agent tool execution needs to happen inside their network, with direct access to source control, internal services, and code repositories.</li>
<li>Agents require custom hardware, such as GPUs or Macs for iOS development, or infrastructure such as Kubernetes, sandboxes, or managed VMs.</li>
<li>Their operating system or build pipeline is difficult to package as a <a href="https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/builds" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">Cloud Agent build</a>.</li>
</ul>
<p>With Self-Hosted Machines, only the execution environment moves while the agent loop, inference, and planning remain in the Cursor cloud. Tool outputs flow back to Cursor for inference and may contain code, and agent transcripts may be processed and stored by Cursor. Teams can continue to access cloud agents from the desktop app, <a href="https://cursor.com/" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">cursor.com</a>, mobile, Slack, GitHub, and Linear.</p>
<figure><div class="media-border-container overflow-hidden"><img alt="Decision guide for when to use Self-Hosted Machines versus Cursor-hosted cloud agents" loading="lazy" width="800" height="450" decoding="async" data-nimg="1" class="media-light transition-opacity duration-[220ms] ease-[var(--ease-out-spring)] will-change-[opacity] opacity-0" style="color:transparent" srcSet="/marketing-static/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fptht05hbb1ssoooe.public.blob.vercel-storage.com%2Fassets%2Fblog%2Fcursor-self-hosted-decision-light-5mb0pPlah9XuRCmn3FSuKKPoaut0lr.png&amp;w=828&amp;q=70 1x, /marketing-static/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fptht05hbb1ssoooe.public.blob.vercel-storage.com%2Fassets%2Fblog%2Fcursor-self-hosted-decision-light-5mb0pPlah9XuRCmn3FSuKKPoaut0lr.png&amp;w=1920&amp;q=70 2x" src="/marketing-static/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fptht05hbb1ssoooe.public.blob.vercel-storage.com%2Fassets%2Fblog%2Fcursor-self-hosted-decision-light-5mb0pPlah9XuRCmn3FSuKKPoaut0lr.png&amp;w=1920&amp;q=70"/><img alt="Decision guide for when to use Self-Hosted Machines versus Cursor-hosted cloud agents" loading="lazy" width="800" height="450" decoding="async" data-nimg="1" class="media-dark transition-opacity duration-[220ms] ease-[var(--ease-out-spring)] will-change-[opacity] opacity-0" style="color:transparent" srcSet="/marketing-static/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fptht05hbb1ssoooe.public.blob.vercel-storage.com%2Fassets%2Fblog%2Fcursor-self-hosted-decision-dark-9pFJZSGCD6lu2MsDVRw6WazC2hLuf7.png&amp;w=828&amp;q=70 1x, /marketing-static/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fptht05hbb1ssoooe.public.blob.vercel-storage.com%2Fassets%2Fblog%2Fcursor-self-hosted-decision-dark-9pFJZSGCD6lu2MsDVRw6WazC2hLuf7.png&amp;w=1920&amp;q=70 2x" src="/marketing-static/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fptht05hbb1ssoooe.public.blob.vercel-storage.com%2Fassets%2Fblog%2Fcursor-self-hosted-decision-dark-9pFJZSGCD6lu2MsDVRw6WazC2hLuf7.png&amp;w=1920&amp;q=70"/></div></figure>
<h2 id="workers-connect-your-infrastructure-to-the-cursor-agent-loop" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#workers-connect-your-infrastructure-to-the-cursor-agent-loop" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Workers connect your infrastructure to the Cursor agent loop</h2>
<p>With Self-Hosted Machines, tool execution moves from a Cursor-hosted VM to a machine in your environment. That machine holds the working copy of the repository, edits files, and runs commands. A worker connects it to the rest of the agent system.</p>
<p>To register a machine, run a worker by installing the Cursor CLI and running <code>agent worker start</code>. This opens a long-lived outbound HTTPS connection to the Cursor cloud. When a session begins, Cursor&#x27;s agent harness handles inference and planning, then sends tool calls to a dedicated worker for execution. The worker returns the results for the next round of inference. Cursor never initiates a connection into your network.</p>
<figure><div class="media-border-container overflow-hidden"><img alt="Architecture diagram showing the Cursor agent loop in the cloud and tool execution on a worker in your network" loading="lazy" width="800" height="450" decoding="async" data-nimg="1" class="media-light transition-opacity duration-[220ms] ease-[var(--ease-out-spring)] will-change-[opacity] opacity-0" style="color:transparent" srcSet="/marketing-static/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fptht05hbb1ssoooe.public.blob.vercel-storage.com%2Fassets%2Fblog%2Fcursor-agent-loop-light-GMamDuzZU5LzYrpQOhRxRwBvrbhRFg.png&amp;w=828&amp;q=70 1x, /marketing-static/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fptht05hbb1ssoooe.public.blob.vercel-storage.com%2Fassets%2Fblog%2Fcursor-agent-loop-light-GMamDuzZU5LzYrpQOhRxRwBvrbhRFg.png&amp;w=1920&amp;q=70 2x" src="/marketing-static/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fptht05hbb1ssoooe.public.blob.vercel-storage.com%2Fassets%2Fblog%2Fcursor-agent-loop-light-GMamDuzZU5LzYrpQOhRxRwBvrbhRFg.png&amp;w=1920&amp;q=70"/><img alt="Architecture diagram showing the Cursor agent loop in the cloud and tool execution on a worker in your network" loading="lazy" width="800" height="450" decoding="async" data-nimg="1" class="media-dark transition-opacity duration-[220ms] ease-[var(--ease-out-spring)] will-change-[opacity] opacity-0" style="color:transparent" srcSet="/marketing-static/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fptht05hbb1ssoooe.public.blob.vercel-storage.com%2Fassets%2Fblog%2Fcursor-agent-loop-dark-qmfnmGC3l8Rw7858QUDT6xB8OuzndD.png&amp;w=828&amp;q=70 1x, /marketing-static/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fptht05hbb1ssoooe.public.blob.vercel-storage.com%2Fassets%2Fblog%2Fcursor-agent-loop-dark-qmfnmGC3l8Rw7858QUDT6xB8OuzndD.png&amp;w=1920&amp;q=70 2x" src="/marketing-static/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fptht05hbb1ssoooe.public.blob.vercel-storage.com%2Fassets%2Fblog%2Fcursor-agent-loop-dark-qmfnmGC3l8Rw7858QUDT6xB8OuzndD.png&amp;w=1920&amp;q=70"/></div></figure>
<figure><div class="media-border-container overflow-hidden"><img alt="Deployment options for cloud agents: Cursor-hosted machines or workers on your servers and public cloud" loading="lazy" width="800" height="450" decoding="async" data-nimg="1" class="media-light transition-opacity duration-[220ms] ease-[var(--ease-out-spring)] will-change-[opacity] opacity-0" style="color:transparent" srcSet="/marketing-static/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fptht05hbb1ssoooe.public.blob.vercel-storage.com%2Fassets%2Fblog%2Fcursor-deployment-options-light-eAVYesILhwbRYnoTFlTDJ4dvUWMszn.png&amp;w=828&amp;q=70 1x, /marketing-static/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fptht05hbb1ssoooe.public.blob.vercel-storage.com%2Fassets%2Fblog%2Fcursor-deployment-options-light-eAVYesILhwbRYnoTFlTDJ4dvUWMszn.png&amp;w=1920&amp;q=70 2x" src="/marketing-static/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fptht05hbb1ssoooe.public.blob.vercel-storage.com%2Fassets%2Fblog%2Fcursor-deployment-options-light-eAVYesILhwbRYnoTFlTDJ4dvUWMszn.png&amp;w=1920&amp;q=70"/><img alt="Deployment options for cloud agents: Cursor-hosted machines or workers on your servers and public cloud" loading="lazy" width="800" height="450" decoding="async" data-nimg="1" class="media-dark transition-opacity duration-[220ms] ease-[var(--ease-out-spring)] will-change-[opacity] opacity-0" style="color:transparent" srcSet="/marketing-static/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fptht05hbb1ssoooe.public.blob.vercel-storage.com%2Fassets%2Fblog%2Fcursor-deployment-options-dark-OZ0kFHszAKB8T4YViL8fRHBnuHnRGw.png&amp;w=828&amp;q=70 1x, /marketing-static/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fptht05hbb1ssoooe.public.blob.vercel-storage.com%2Fassets%2Fblog%2Fcursor-deployment-options-dark-OZ0kFHszAKB8T4YViL8fRHBnuHnRGw.png&amp;w=1920&amp;q=70 2x" src="/marketing-static/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fptht05hbb1ssoooe.public.blob.vercel-storage.com%2Fassets%2Fblog%2Fcursor-deployment-options-dark-OZ0kFHszAKB8T4YViL8fRHBnuHnRGw.png&amp;w=1920&amp;q=70"/></div></figure>
<p>Workers can be configured in two ways.</p>
<ol>
<li><strong>My Machines.</strong> This configuration connects a single laptop or VM to your account and is best suited to personal workflows.</li>
<li><strong>Pools.</strong> A pool is a named queue of workers that can serve a team or enterprise. Capacity increases as requests arrive and decreases after workers disconnect, letting your existing cloud infrastructure scale with developer demand.</li>
</ol>
<div class="card mb-v2"><blockquote class="not-prose"><p class="type-base whitespace-pre-wrap">Developers should have the flexibility to run coding agents on the platform that best supports their workflow, and companies should not have to compromise on control of where agents run and what they can access. The future of development will be built on powerful agents, running in secure, isolated environments.</p></blockquote><div class="mt-v1 flex items-center space-x-(--grid-gap)"><div><div class="type-sm">Meagan Gamache</div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text-sec">Director of Product Management, Developer Platforms<!-- -->, <!-- -->Cloudflare</div></div></div></div>
<h2 id="cloud-agents-adapt-to-your-infrastructure" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#cloud-agents-adapt-to-your-infrastructure" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Cloud agents adapt to your infrastructure</h2>
<p>Worker pools can now scale in response to queued requests and serve work from any repository. We have also added support for several sandbox providers and computer use on Linux alongside Mac.</p>
<h3 id="pools-scale-with-demand-and-serve-any-repository" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#pools-scale-with-demand-and-serve-any-repository" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Pools scale with demand and serve any repository</h3>
<p>Demand for cloud agents often arrives in bursts and Self-Hosted Machines pools adjust to those bursts automatically. This happens through a controller which watches the request queue and uses a spawn script supplied by the team to start machines as needed.</p>
<p>If a pool has an available worker, that worker claims the request. Otherwise, the request waits until more capacity becomes available, so teams do not have to decide how many machines to leave running.</p>
<p>Teams can set an idle timeout for each worker connection. Once it expires, the machine can reset and re-enter the pool. Teams can also preserve its workspace in case the agent receives a follow-up.</p>
<div class="card mb-v2"><blockquote class="not-prose"><p class="type-base whitespace-pre-wrap">Self-Hosted Machines put teams in control of where Cursor agents run, and Vercel Sandbox makes it effortless. Every task gets an isolated sandbox on demand, no fleet to manage, and nothing sitting idle.</p></blockquote><div class="mt-v1 flex items-center space-x-(--grid-gap)"><div><div class="type-sm">Allen Zhou</div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text-sec">Member of Technical Staff<!-- -->, <!-- -->Vercel</div></div></div></div>
<p>Leaving a machine running while its agent is idle can be expensive. But if the machine is released, the agent may need several minutes to reconstruct its workspace when a follow-up arrives. With hibernation, teams can snapshot and stop an idle machine instead. If a follow-up arrives within the reconnect window, the snapshot is restored and a worker starts with the same ID. Otherwise, the request can move to a new machine.</p>
<p>Pools are not tied to individual repositories. A request only needs to identify the pool, and any available worker can claim it. This lets one pool serve many repositories.</p>
<h3 id="workers-run-across-supported-sandbox-providers" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#workers-run-across-supported-sandbox-providers" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Workers run across supported sandbox providers</h3>
<p>Self-Hosted Machines does not require building a custom sandbox layer from scratch. We partner with <a href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/microvms-integrations-cursor-self-hosted-machines.html" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">AWS Lambda</a>, <a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/sandbox/tutorials/cursor-cloud-agents/" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">Cloudflare</a>, <a href="https://coder.com/docs/ai-coder/agent-relay/cursor" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">Coder</a>, <a href="https://daytona.io/docs/en/guides/cursor/cursor-self-hosted-machines" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">Daytona</a>, <a href="https://docs.e2b.dev/agents/cursor" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">E2B</a>, <a href="https://modal.com/docs/cursor" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">Modal</a>, <a href="https://namespace.so/docs/integrations/cursor" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">Namespace</a>, and <a href="https://vercel.com/kb/guide/cursor-vercel-sandbox" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">Vercel</a>, allowing workers to be started and orchestrated wherever a team&#x27;s sandboxes already run.</p>
<div class="card mb-v2"><blockquote class="not-prose"><p class="type-base whitespace-pre-wrap">Cursor Self-Hosted Machines on Modal gives each Cloud Agent session a Modal Sandbox, so you can hand it a machine tailor-made for its task.</p></blockquote><div class="mt-v1 flex items-center space-x-(--grid-gap)"><div><div class="type-sm">Adam Azzam</div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text-sec">Member of Product Staff<!-- -->, <!-- -->Modal</div></div></div></div>
<h3 id="agents-control-browsers-on-linux-and-mac" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#agents-control-browsers-on-linux-and-mac" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Agents control browsers on Linux and Mac</h3>
<p>Linux workers now support computer use alongside Macs. With the required <a href="https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/self-hosted/computer-use" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">computer use</a> dependencies installed, including Chrome or Chromium, an agent can click, take screenshots, and control the browser. You can watch its desktop or take control directly from Cursor.</p>
<div class="card mb-v2"><blockquote class="not-prose"><p class="type-base whitespace-pre-wrap">You can&#x27;t build iOS or macOS apps without a Mac. Namespace Devboxes spin up a real Mac for each Cursor Cloud Agent, which can now perform that work on Apple silicon.</p></blockquote><div class="mt-v1 flex items-center space-x-(--grid-gap)"><div><div class="type-sm">Hugo Santos</div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text-sec">CEO<!-- -->, <!-- -->Namespace</div></div></div></div>
<h2 id="bring-cloud-agents-into-your-environment" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#bring-cloud-agents-into-your-environment" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Bring cloud agents into your environment</h2>
<p>Teams have spent years shaping their infrastructure around how they build software. Self-Hosted Machines lets cloud agents fit more naturally into it, and we&#x27;re excited to see how far teams take them.</p>
<p>To connect a machine or configure a pool, <a href="https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/self-hosted" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">get started in the docs</a>.</p></div><footer
